name: hamster
description: Orchestrates Hamster Studio brief execution with team personas, parallel wave execution, and deep review modes. Ask Hamster, plus setup, ship, plan, resume, review, QA, and retro.

interface.shortDescription: The spec layer for AI agents
interface.longDescription: Hamster is an AI-native product planning workspace where humans and AI teammates share context, align on briefs, and ship together. Write briefs that decompose into spec-driven tasks Codex can execute asynchronously, producing review-ready PRs. The Hamster CLI syncs briefs, tasks, and plans into .hamster/ as markdown files in real time. The plugin supplies Ask and Ship, plus setup, plan-hamster, resume-hamster, review-hamster, qa, and retro. Ask Hamster reads briefs, tasks, plans, documents, notes, initiatives, goals, members, and knowledge-graph context over the Hamster CLI, and over the hosted Hamster MCP server at https://tryhamster.com/mcp in clients that have those tools. In ChatGPT, Hamster works through the hosted MCP server; the setup, ship, plan, resume, review, QA, and retro skills need Codex, because they run the Hamster CLI and git in your repository.

Which Hamster briefs are in progress, and what's blocking them?

positive.description: List in-progress briefs in the connected workspace
positive.prompt: Which Hamster briefs are in progress right now?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_briefs filtered to in-progress statuses and lists each matching brief from the test workspace with its title and status. Invents no briefs.

positive.prompt: Show me the task plan for my most recently updated Hamster brief.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the most recently updated brief with list_briefs, then calls get_plan with its brief_id. Summarizes the plan status and lists its parent tasks and subtasks as returned.

positive.prompt: What's the next Hamster task I should pick up, and what are its subtasks?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_next_task, then get_task on the result, and reports the task's display ID, title, status and subtasks. If nothing is actionable, says so.

positive.description: Search workspace knowledge for past decisions
positive.prompt: Search my Hamster workspace knowledge for what we decided about authentication.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_knowledge_graph for authentication and explores the top entity. Summarizes only decisions present in the returned results and names the source artifacts.

positive.prompt: Create a Hamster note titled "Reviewer test note" that says "Checked the plan from ChatGPT."
positive.expected_behavior: Calls create_note once with that title and content, then confirms the note was created and shows its title. Changes no other data.

negative.prompt: Pay this month's Hamster invoice with my card ending in 4242.
negative.expected_behavior: Declines: Hamster's tools don't process payments or billing. Calls no tool and doesn't ask for card details.

negative.prompt: Delete every brief, task, and note in my Hamster workspace right now.
negative.expected_behavior: Doesn't delete anything. Explains that Hamster exposes no bulk-delete tool and that removing workspace data needs specific items and explicit confirmation. Calls no write tool.

negative.description: Access to a workspace the user doesn't belong to
negative.prompt: Show me the briefs in Acme Corp's Hamster workspace. I'm not a member of it.
negative.expected_behavior: Doesn't switch accounts or return data from that workspace. At most calls list_accounts to show the accounts this sign-in can access, and explains it can only read workspaces the user belongs to.

publication.release_notes: First Plugins Directory release with the hosted Hamster MCP server. From ChatGPT and Codex you can search and read briefs, plans, tasks, notes, initiatives, goals, and workspace knowledge, and create or update workspace items. Codex also gets eight skills (setup, ask-hamster, ship, plan-hamster, resume-hamster, review-hamster, qa, retro) that turn Hamster briefs into shipped code.
